status_vocabulary.PATCHED_AND_TESTED: Vulnerable version removed from every listed graph and tests executed on the remediation commit
status_vocabulary.NOT_APPLICABLE_WITH_APPROVED_EVIDENCE: Requires a human approval record; evidence alone is a PROPOSAL
status_vocabulary.FORMALLY_ACCEPTED_RESIDUAL_RISK: Requires a human approval record with compensating controls
status_vocabulary.UNRESOLVED: No fix and no approved disposition; blocks the gate

gate_rule: s35_supply_chain stays FAIL while any finding is UNRESOLVED or NOT_VERIFIED, or any cargo-audit/cargo-deny command exits non-zero
gate_effect: None. s35_supply_chain still consumes raw scanner exit codes and the Sprint 37 evaluator still reads the Sprint 37 matrix. This file is a review package only.

findings.upgrade_blocked_by: holochain_data 0.7.1 requires libsqlite3-sys ^0.35 and sqlx-sqlite 0.9.0 (latest) requires <0.38.0; resolver rejects 0.39.1. Even libsqlite3-sys 0.39.x bundled-sqlcipher (sqlcipher-src =419.0.6, SQLite 3.53.4) remains affected per the advisory, so a version bump would NOT fix encrypted Holochain databases.

reachability.features: holochain_data `encryption` -> rusqlite bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl; libsqlite3-sys builds SQLCipher 4.6.1 (SQLite 3.46.1), not the 3.50.2 plain bundle
reachability.attack_preconditions: Local actor able to write a database file AND a sibling -wal with mismatched page size into the conductor data root, then the conductor opens it
reachability.exposure: Disclosure of uninitialised page-cache bytes from the conductor process to query results
reachability.untrusted_input_path: No network path. Relevant to restore-from-backup if backup media/WAL files are less trusted than the conductor.

findings.proposed_rationale: Local-only precondition requires write access to the conductor data root, which already implies full compromise of conductor state. No compatible patched SQLCipher exists upstream. Accept only with compensating controls.
compensating_controls_required: Conductor data root owned by the conductor service account, mode 0700
Backups taken only after WAL checkpoint; restore procedure rejects stray -wal/-shm files and verifies SHA-256 manifests before open
Do not run in-process (danger) Lair keystore in production; keys stay in separate lair-keystore process
regression_tests_required: Restore rejects backup containing unexpected -wal sibling
Corrupt offline backup rejection (Sprint 33) re-run on final SHA
findings.residual_risk: Local information disclosure if data-root write isolation fails
findings.next_action: Owner decision on residual-risk acceptance; request SQLCipher >= 4.12 / SQLite >= 3.54 path from Holochain upstream (holochain_data)

sprint38.applicable_features: holochain default `encryption` -> libsqlite3-sys bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl (shared by holochain_data/sqlx and lair_keystore/rusqlite)
runtime_evidence: Compiled core identified in the 0.7.1 binary: SQLITE_SOURCE_ID 2024-08-13 c9c2ab54... = SQLite 3.46.1 / SQLCipher 4.6.1

Advisory requires SQLite >= 3.54.0; RustSec marks libsqlite3-sys >= 0.39.0 patched, but with bundled-sqlcipher 0.39.x uses sqlcipher-src 419.0.6 (SQLite 3.53.4) and stays affected; first fixed SQLCipher build is libsqlite3-sys 0.40.0 (sqlcipher-src 420.0.0, SQLite 3.54.1, released 2026-11-11)
holochain_data 0.7.1 applies per-database key + salt, cipher_plaintext_header_size=32, WAL mode, trusted_schema=false
Whether SQLCipher's per-page HMAC rejects a page-size-mismatched WAL before the uninitialised read is NOT tested
compensating_controls: scripts/security/datastore_guard.py audit-root: data root owned by service uid, 0700/0600, no symlinks/hard links (implemented, 10 tests)
datastore_guard.py make-manifest/verify-restore: restores reject any -wal/-shm/-journal, unlisted, tampered or symlinked files (implemented, tested)
Backups must be WAL-checkpointed (PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)) with writers stopped (operator procedure; not enforced by code)
sprint38.residual_risk: Local information disclosure if data-root write isolation fails
sprint38.upstream_remediation_dependency: Holochain release on libsqlite3-sys >= 0.40.0 with bundled-sqlcipher; blocked today by holochain_data ^0.35 and sqlx-sqlite 0.9.0 (<0.38)
sprint38.approval_status: NOT_APPROVED — no human approval record exists

findings.behaviour: Holochain's `encryption` feature compiles SQLCipher 4.6.1 based on SQLite 3.46.1 (2024-08-13). RustSec maps libsqlite3-sys 0.35.0 to the plain SQLite 3.50.2 bundle, so SQLite C CVEs fixed between 3.46.1 and 3.50.2 are not flagged for the SQLCipher build. Only two libsqlite3-sys advisories exist in RustSec.
findings.scanner_visibility: NOT REPORTED: scanner version mapping does not model the bundled-sqlcipher amalgamation

evidence: libsqlite3-sys-0.35.0/sqlcipher/sqlite3.c: SQLITE_VERSION 3.46.1, CIPHER_VERSION_NUMBER 4.6.1
libsqlite3-sys-0.35.0/sqlite3/sqlite3.c: SQLITE_VERSION 3.50.2
cargo tree -e features: holochain_data feature encryption -> bundled-sqlcipher-vendored-openssl

findings.proposed_rationale: Reviewer must enumerate sqlite.org/cves.html for fixes after 3.46.1 and assess each (most require attacker-controlled SQL; Holochain issues its own prepared statements).
findings.residual_risk: Unknown until enumerated
findings.next_action: Independent reviewer enumerates SQLite CVEs > 3.46.1 against SQLCipher 4.6.1

runtime_evidence: Post-3.46.1 core CVEs per sqlite.org/cves.html: CVE-2025-3277/29087 (concat_ws, 3.49.1), CVE-2025-29088/52099 (lookaside config, 3.49.1), CVE-2025-6965 (aggregate column overflow, 3.50.2), CVE-2025-7709 (FTS5 corrupt index, 3.50.3), CVE-2026-11822/11824 (FTS5 heap write with DEFENSIVE off, 3.53.2), CVE-2026-119375 (WAL page size, 3.54.0)
Source diff against the bundled 3.50.2 amalgamation confirms the concat_ws (i64 cast), lookaside clamp and findOrCreateAggInfoColumn mxTerm fixes are ABSENT from the compiled 3.46.1 core

FTS3/FTS5 and load_extension are compiled in; no Holochain/Lair crate references concat_ws, FTS5, SQLITE_DBCONFIG_LOOKASIDE or extension loading; zomes cannot submit SQL; trusted_schema=false limits functions in crafted schemas

Exploitation of the SQL-level CVEs needs arbitrary SQL or a crafted database; the remaining open question is crafted-database input (data-root write or restore), which the datastore guard addresses but does not eliminate
compensating_controls: datastore_guard.py data-root audit and restore validation (implemented, tested)
SQLITE_DBCONFIG_DEFENSIVE status of Holochain connections NOT verified
